component.name: KAthenaeum
component.summary: Offline Wikipedia library with a local AI research assistant

description.p: KAthenaeum turns Kiwix ZIM files into a searchable library on your own computer. Ask a question and get an answer written by a small local language model, with every sentence linked back to the Wikipedia article it came from.
Features:

ul.li: Read and search offline Wikipedia, and any other Wikipedia-style library from the Kiwix catalog
Ask questions answered from your libraries, with citations computed by the application and unsupported sentences flagged
A classroom: an AI teacher plans courses from your libraries, with lesson introductions, quizzes, unit tests and a tutor
Research projects with sources, saved passages, notes, a project chat and Markdown documents
Highlights and notes, citations in MLA, APA and Chicago style, a dictionary and timelines
A map whose places open their Wikipedia articles, with towns and cities kept for use offline

description.p: Your libraries work entirely offline, and the AI runs on your computer through Ollama: no cloud service, no account and no tracking. The internet is used only for the library catalog, downloads and the map, and can be switched off.

description.p: Wikibooks and Wikiversity pages show the way back to their book (“‹ Cell Biology › Cell division”), and from the book's page to its other chapters.

The Classroom's teacher reads open textbooks too: installed Wikibooks and Wikiversity chapters become lesson readings for every subject, a book written for the learner's level preferred to one for another, and a book's contents pages and printable versions left out.

The map is now drawn by Marble, KDE's map library, from KDE's map server: no region downloads needed. Areas you view are kept as you go, and Keep This Area Offline keeps a whole town or city. Clicking a place still opens its Wikipedia article. A new setting turns the internet off entirely; the catalog, downloads and the map then work from what is on the computer.

Timelines: every dated sentence of an article, or of a research project's articles, in date order under its period, from "14 October 1066" to "7,700 years ago". Each event is the article's own sentence and opens it; a timeline can be kept in a project or exported.

Classroom: lesson quizzes and unit tests written from the readings, each answer checked against the passage it comes from, graded with the right answer and the passage; scores on the course page and a list of what to review. Ask Your Teacher: a chat on every lesson that guides with hints and questions rather than handing over answers.

Classroom: a lesson's readings open with the lesson beside them, its questions first. A course can be kept in a research project: its readings become sources marked with their lesson, each introduction a document to answer in, and what you highlight while reading is saved there too.

The Classroom: tell it about yourself, choose a subject (or any topic) and a level, and an AI teacher plans a course of units and lessons. Each lesson reads real articles from your libraries, chosen for being about it, with an introduction written for you. Lessons with nothing to read are left out rather than made up, and missing libraries are pointed out.

Tools for studying: highlight passages in four colours and write notes on them, gathered on a Notes page; cite any article in MLA, APA or Chicago style, with a bibliography for each project and works cited added to exported documents; look up a word in an installed Wiktionary from the right-click menu; and show the place an article is about on your maps.

A handbook in KDE's Help Center. A more current look: a sidebar with search, page titles in the header, cards, compact buttons and segmented tabs. Map regions chosen by their shapes, the map reopening where it was left, articles across the whole window, and a check for newer versions of your libraries.
Research projects: have the AI write a report to your own instructions, planned in sections, each written from the sources that fit it, with citations and a reference list added by KAthenaeum.
Offline maps: download the world overview and the regions you choose in Settings, browse them without a connection, and click a place to open its Wikipedia article from your libraries.
Project documents open in a window of their own with Kate's editor: Markdown highlighting, spell check, search and replace, vi mode, beside a live preview.

A full review: the interface can no longer reach the network except the Kiwix catalog, oversized or hostile library files are refused, removing a library while searching no longer crashes, answers and drafts keep going when you leave their page, and many smaller fixes. A new icon.
Projects: AI-drafted summaries and chat notes, saved passages highlighted in their articles, and your notes shown in a document's preview.
Research projects: collect articles, saved passages, answers and chats with notes; ask questions answered from the project; write Markdown documents that cite its sources, and export them.
Ask about this article: a chat panel beside every article that answers from that article alone, with citations to its sections. Ask about selected text.
Ask: answers from your libraries written by a local model, with every sentence linked to its source and unsupported sentences flagged. Follow-up questions, saved chats, and model settings.
Search: titles as you type, then the text of every article in every library, with the matching passage shown.
Library Manager: browse the Kiwix catalog, download and verify libraries, manage installed ones. Reading: library home, A to Z, and articles with their pictures.
